subject: EOQ OKR concordance: final scores, callouts, and comms ask
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: dana.park@atlasanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EOQ OKR concordance: draft scores + evidence request

Team —

We need to close the EOQ scoring this week so the QBR materials can go to comms next Tuesday. I pulled a first pass and attached an evidence pack (EOQ_evidence_pack.pdf) with supporting links. Quick asks:

- Please review the annotated scores in OKR-score-annotated.xlsx and flag any objections by EOD Monday (Sep 13).
- If you disagree with a score, add a 1-2 line rationale and point to the evidence page in the pack.
- Laura — can you lead a 30m sync Monday morning to reconcile disparities?

High-level: most objectives land where we'd expected, but there are 3 cross-functional callouts (customer latency, model-cost per 1K tokens, and rollout cadence) that need explicit decisions. If we don't close these, the comms draft will have to include a delayed action item rather than a firm commit.

Attachments: EOQ_evidence_pack.pdf, OKR-score-annotated.xlsx

Thanks —
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EOQ OKR concordance: draft scores + evidence request

Rohan —

Thanks for pulling this together. I reviewed the workbook and left inline notes on three objectives:

1) Customer latency (OBJ-3): bump from 7 -> 8 based on new Aurora region benchmarks (see page 4 of evidence pack).
2) Model-cost per 1K tokens (OBJ-5): keep at 6; our cost improvement is still below the threshold we set.
3) Rollout cadence (OBJ-8): propose a half-point uplift (5.5) to reflect two successful dedicated rollouts but one missed canary.

I can host a 30m reconciliation tomorrow at 9:30 PT. Agenda: a) reconcile these three callouts, b) lock final scores, c) agree comms language for the customer-facing section.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rohan.mehta@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EOQ OKR concordance: draft scores + evidence request

On Fri, Sep 10, 2027 at 11:03 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rohan —
> 
> Thanks for pulling this together. I reviewed the workbook and left inline notes on three objectives:
> 
> 1) Customer latency (OBJ-3): bump from 7 -> 8 based on new Aurora region benchmarks (see page 4 of evidence pack).
> 2) Model-cost per 1K tokens (OBJ-5): keep at 6; our cost improvement is still below the threshold we set.
> 3) Rollout cadence (OBJ-8): propose a half-point uplift (5.5) to reflect two successful dedicated rollouts but one missed canary.

Thanks, Laura — I agree with (1) but want to call out nuance on (3). The missed canary was caused by a third-party infra flake (see evidence pack appendix) and the product rollout met internal gating otherwise. My suggestion: keep the half point but add an explicit callout in the narrative that the canary failure was external and that we have a mitigation plan (infra retry + extended sim). That keeps the score without implying internal process failure.

Also adding one practical ask for the comms draft: please avoid technical jargon in the customer-facing line for OBJ-5; customers care about cost directionality, not quantized per-token deltas.

- Priyom
Principal PM, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Dana Park <dana.park@atlasanalytics.com>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EOQ OKR concordance: draft scores + evidence request

Rohan / Laura —

Quick note from the Atlas side: the Aurora latency bench noted on page 4 was coordinated with our infra team; we're comfortable with the reported uplift and happy to be cited in the QBR. One small ask — in the customer-facing QBR paragraph could you say "average API latency improved 12% in our Aurora region" rather than specifying p95 numbers? That wording resonates more with our execs.

Happy to jump on the call if useful.

Thanks,
Dana Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Atlas Analytics

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: dana.park@atlasanalytics.com, zane@atlasanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EOQ OKR concordance: draft scores + evidence request

Team —

Thanks for the fast turn. Summary / decisions to close the loop: 

- OBJ-3 (Customer latency): final = 8. Laura's uplift accepted; we will use customer-forward wording from Dana: "average API latency improved 12% in our Aurora region."
- OBJ-5 (Model-cost per 1K tokens): final = 6. Keep phrasing high-level for comms.
- OBJ-8 (Rollout cadence): final = 5.5 with explicit bullet in the narrative noting the external infra cause and the mitigation plan (infra retry + extended sim).

Next steps (owners & due dates):
- Laura: run the 30m reconciliation tomorrow 9:30 PT to capture any lingering edits and produce the final OKR table (Deliverable: OKR-score-annotated.xlsx updated) — due Tue Sep 14 EOD.
- Marissa: fold final lines into QBR-comms-draft.docx and share with comms for review — due Wed Sep 15 EOD.
- Priyom: add the 1-2 sentence mitigation summary into the rollout narrative section — due Tue Sep 14 noon PT.
- Rohan: once final files are in, I will produce the comms email and the exec one-pager.

Attachments included for distribution: EOQ_evidence_pack.pdf, OKR-score-annotated.xlsx, QBR-comms-draft.docx

If there are no disputes by Tue EOD I will mark these scores as final and publish the QBR packet.

—
